name: Question 20
problem: Consider the thin plate $D$ enclosed between the curve $x={y}^{2}$ and the $y$-axis for $-2\le y\le 0.$ Given that the area of the plate is $\frac{8}{3},$ find the $y$-coordinate of its centroid.
worked_solution:
The centroid of a lamina $D$ with area ${A}_{D}$ is given by $({x}_{c},{y}_{c}),$ where

$$
{x}_{c}=\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}x\,\,\text{d}A,\,{y}_{c}=\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}y\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that $D$ is a type II plane region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/a8c57b12334a23542bae73ba1ac6848e69830b9663a1f83b6340f6812974f416.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le {y}^{2},\,-2\le y\le 0}
$$

and ${A}_{D}=\frac{8}{3}.$

Therefore, the $y$-coordinate of the centroid is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{c} & =\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{3}{8}{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}y\,\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{8}{\int }_{-2}^{0}y\,{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{8}{\int }_{-2}^{0}y[x]_{x=0}^{x={y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{8}{\int }_{-2}^{0}y({y}^{2}-0)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{8}{\int }_{-2}^{0}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{8}{[\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}]}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =\frac{3}{8}\cdot (0-4) \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Correct
EXPLANATION

The centroid of a lamina D with area AD is given by (xc,yc), where

xc=1AD∬DxdA,yc=1AD∬DydA.

Notice that D is a type II plane region:

So, we have

D={(x,y):0≤x≤y2,−2≤y≤0}

and AD=83.

Therefore, the y-coordinate of the centroid is

yc=1AD∬DydA=38∫−20∫0y2ydxdy=38∫−20y∫0y2dxdy=38∫−20y[x]x=0x=y2dy=38∫−20y(y2−0)dy=38∫−20y3dy=38[y44]−20=38⋅(0−4)=−32.
